newsitem.title: SYRIA: France sees obstacles still blocking Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: France sees obstacles still blocking Mideast peace.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Wednesday obstacles were still blocking the revival of Syrian-Israeli peace talks which broke off a year ago.

Speaking to reporters on arrival in Damascus from Israel, where he had talks with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other Israeli leaders, de Charette said Paris would continue its efforts to achieve progress.

"As you know there are many obstacles which are blocking the way of peace and France will try to solve these problems. I give big importance to the talks that I will have here with President Hafez al-Assad," de Charette said.
Officials said the French minister, on a regional tour that would take him also to Lebanon, would meet his Syrian counterpart Farouq al-Shara and President Assad on Thursday.
Speaking to reporters at the airport Shara said that de Charette's talks in Syria would help achieve progress on the peace process.
"We are sure that de Charette's talks in Damascus will be fruitful and constructive and will help advance the peace process which is at a standstill at present," Shara said.
Shara renewed Damascus' demands to resume the peace talks with Israel at the point where they left off under Israel's previous government.
Syria says that Israel's Labour-led government had agreed during talks with Damascus to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.
Israel has held sporadic peace talks with Syria since 1991 but the negotiations, which broke off in March 1996, did not achieve progress.
Syria strongly condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace and refused his offer to resume the talks without conditions.

The Syrian foreign minister blasted Netanyahu again on Wednesday and accused him of working against peace by endorsing plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews in east Jerusalem, where Palestinians hope to build a capital for a future state.
"The Israeli measures do not help peace. They give the practical evidence that Netanyahu does not want peace and does not even bother about world opinion," Shara said.
